mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS level at the decision date (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs signals labor market strength that reduces uncertainty, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 decision windows where PAYEMS > 50000, less than 40% of 20-day forward returns are positive (binomial test p > 0.4).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates improving supply capacity while curbing cost pressures, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction term between INDPRO and CPIAUCSL is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression predicting 5-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months indicates an over-supplied housing market, which lowers long-term growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of dual consecutive monthly declines in HOUST, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, it signals a tightening labor market that the Federal Reserve interprets as a signal for higher for longer rates, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% after a 3-month decline
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE crosses below 4.5% with a downward trend, 60-day forward returns remain positive (p < 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 jobs, occurring during a period of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), suggests resilient labor demand without cost pressures and is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: labor demand growth with deflationary pressures
failure_condition: The interaction between PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL is not predictive of 20-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.01 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate easing price pressures while improving supply, which together form a non-inflationary demand expansion that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months while INDPRO increases
failure_condition: The combined effect of CPIAUCSL and INDPRO is not predictive of 5-day forward returns (p > 0.05 in logistic regression).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive momentum effect in the S&P 500 forward returns is present when the 12-month moving average of GDP deflator inflation (not directly observable here) is below 2%, regardless of other macro signals, producing positive returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: low inflation regime (assumed from CPIAUCSL behavior)
failure_condition: In low-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL < 205), less than 60% of 20-day forward returns are positive (binomial test).
